newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA COTTON LIFTS ON LIMITED SUPPLIES, QUOTA HOPES.
newsitem.headline: INDIA COTTON LIFTS ON LIMITED SUPPLIES, QUOTA HOPES.

text.p: Cotton prices lifted further on Wednesday on limited supplies and traders' hopes that the Indian government would relax export quotas, despite slow mill buying on Wednesday, dealers said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose to 1,125/1,160 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) from 1,070/1,120 rupees. Punjab saw-ginned moved up by 30 rupees to 1,825/1,900 rupees per maund.
"Indian government may allow more export of cotton for some of the state-owned agencies which are nursing unsold stock at the tail-end of the season," one broker said.

India has authorised an export quota of 1.34 million bales (170 kg each) for the current cotton season. Of these, 1.15 million bales have been registered and actual shipment so far has been 900,000 bales.

In the Gujarat segment Kalyan cotton rose by 100 rupees to 14,500/15,100 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Kala-ginned rose by 100 rupees at 12,700 rupees and Wagad by 100 rupees at 13,500/13,600 rupees per candy.
